title: GPU Capacity & Infrastructure Runbook
author: Asha Patel
summary: Operational runbook for handling GPU fleet capacity, cloud accounts & networking impacts, Terraform/IaC module changes, and CI/CD deployment steps. Includes monitoring, alert thresholds, immediate remediation, and long-term capacity planning.
content:
Purpose:
This runbook describes standard operating procedures for detecting, mitigating, and remediating GPU capacity and related infrastructure incidents that affect Redwood inference workloads (hosted, dedicated, private). It covers alerts, immediate actions, Terraform/IaC touchpoints, CI/CD steps for emergency fixes, and long-term capacity planning.

Scope:
- GPU fleet capacity (pools, nodegroups, ASGs, spot/ondemand mixes)
- Cloud accounts and networking impacts that affect capacity (VPC quotas, ENI limits, IAM permissions for provisioning)
- Terraform / IaC modules that define GPU pools and autoscaling policies
- CI/CD pipelines for infra changes (Terraform plans, apply gates, release approvals)
- Relevant runbooks for rolling upgrades and rollback

Ownership and Contacts:
- On-call owner: eng-infra oncall rotation (pager: #eng-infra-oncall)
- Primary owner: Asha Patel (infra lead)
- Secondary owner: Miguel Alvarez (capacity eng)
- Escalation: Eng SRE manager -> Head of Infrastructure -> VP Eng (follow internal escalation matrix)

Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Thresholds:
| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Measurement window | Alert name |
|-------|-------------------:|-------------------:|--------------------:|-----------|
| GPU pool utilization (usable GPUs / licensed GPUs) | 75% | 90% | 5m average | gpu_pool_high_util_warning / gpu_pool_high_util_critical |
| Pending pods requiring GPU | > 5 pods pending | > 20 pods pending | 5m | gpu_pods_pending_warning / gpu_pods_pending_critical |
| Queue latency (inference request time in queue) | 150ms p95 | 500ms p95 | 5m | inference_queue_latency_warning / inference_queue_latency_critical |
| Cloud capacity error rate (API quota/ENI/limit errors) | 0.5% | 2% | 10m | cloud_api_quota_errors_warning / cloud_api_quota_errors_critical |

Monitoring and Alerts (where to look):
- Prometheus / Cortex alerts: gpu_pool_high_util_*, gpu_pods_pending_*, inference_queue_latency_*, cloud_api_quota_errors_*
- Grafana dashboards: "GPU Fleet Overview", "GPU Pool by Region", "Pending Workloads", "Autoscaler Decisions"
- Pager duty: eng-infra-oncall
- Slack channels: #eng-infra-alerts (for automated alerts), #eng-infra-ops (for coordination)

Immediate Triage (first 10 minutes):
1. Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and post an incident channel in #eng-infra-ops with the alert link, approximate impact (e.g., number of customers affected), and primary owner.
2. Check dashboards for scope: which regions, which GPU pools, and which services (hosted/dedicated/private) are impacted.
3. Run quick health checks:
   - kubectl get pods -A | grep Pending | grep gpu
   - kubectl describe pod <example-pod> to see scheduling errors (e.g., Insufficient GPU / nodeSelector mismatch)
   - Check cloud provider API error rates: aws cloudwatch metrics / gcp monitoring
4. If the issue is "Pending pods due to Insufficient GPUs": follow the "Scale up" path below.
5. If cloud API quota or ENI/attachment errors are present, follow the "Cloud quota / networking" path below.

Immediate Mitigation Paths:
A. Scale up (fastest path - best effort):
- Goal: add capacity in affected region(s) to reduce pending pods and lower latency.
- Options (in order of preference):
  1. Increase Karpenter / Cluster Autoscaler limits (if hitting ASG/scale-down limits). Quick command example (AWS):
     - aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name <asg-name> --max-size <new-max> --desired-capacity <new-desired>
  2. Trigger an on-demand burst pool (pre-provisioned ondemand pool) if configured:
     - Terraform-managed: see module path modules/gpu_pool -> var.ondemand_burst_enabled (see Terraform section).
  3. Convert some spot pools to on-demand for short-lived surge. Use console or IaC to switch allocation strategy.
  4. If a pre-warmed pool exists for dedicated customers, route traffic to the pre-warmed pool via routing policy.
- Post-action: verify pending pods drain and p95 queue latency falls below warning threshold.

B. Re-route traffic (service-level mitigation):
- If the platform supports model variants and regional fallback, change routing policy to a compatible model variant in a different region/instance type: update routing policy in the control plane (Console -> Routing -> Canary / Fallback).
- For high-priority customers on Dedicated: promote requests to dedicated reserved capacity if available.

C. Cloud quota or ENI/Networking limits:
- Symptoms: API errors when provisioning nodes, ENI attach failures, IAM access denied, or VPC subnet exhaustion.
- Steps:
  1. Check cloud provider console for quota errors (AWS Service Quotas, GCP Quotas).
  2. If ENI limits: reduce pods-per-node by adjusting kubelet max pods or increase instance size (larger instance increases ENIs).
  3. Open emergency support ticket with cloud provider if quota increase is required and internal rate not sufficient.
  4. Temporary workaround: shift workload to a region with available quotas and update routing rules.

Terraform / IaC Touchpoints (what to change for a persistent fix):
- Primary modules and repositories (examples):
  - infra/modules/gpu_pool (defines nodegroups, instance_types, spot/ondemand mix, autoscaling settings)
  - infra/modules/networking (VPC subnets, ENI/pod density, route tables)
  - infra/modules/cloud_accounts (IAM roles, quotas, service-linked roles)
  - infra/overlays/region-*/gpu-pool.tf (region-specific overrides)
- Best practices when making changes:
  1. Never make long-lived manual changes to cloud infra without a Terraform plan and peer review. Short-lived emergency on-console changes must be reconciled into IaC immediately.
  2. Write a focused Terraform change: update module.gpu_pool.max_size or add ondemand_burst_count variable.
  3. Run terraform plan in the infra CI (see CI/CD section) and get approvals.

Example Terraform change snippet (stringified file to apply):
  module "gpu_pool" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-modules.git//gpu_pool?ref=main"
    region = "us-west-2"
    instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge", "g5.12xlarge"]
    spot = true
    max_size = 200
    ondemand_burst_enabled = true
    ondemand_burst_count = 20
  }

CI/CD and Approval Flow (emergency and normal):
- Pipelines:
  - repo: infra/terraform (GitHub) -> workflow: terraform-plan-apply.yml (GitHub Actions)
  - job: plan -> approval -> apply (apply is gated by infra-owners and oncall for emergency)
  - quick patch flow: "hotfix-terraform" branch with required reviewers = oncall + infra owner
- Emergency procedure (fastest safe path):
  1. Create a branch hotfix/<short-desc> and commit minimal change (e.g., max_size var).
  2. Trigger GitHub Actions plan; post plan to PR and tag oncall reviewer.
  3. If PR approval cannot be obtained in time, use the documented emergency apply policy: senior infra engineer may run terraform apply with explicit state backup and notify stakeholders immediately. Record all manual steps in the incident ticket.
  4. After emergency manual apply, follow up with a reconciled PR to ensure IaC matches cloud state.

Rollback and Post-incident Cleanup:
- If scaling caused unexpected cost/spare capacity issues, revert Terraform change to previous values and run terraform apply.
- Ensure any temporary on-console changes are committed to IaC and PR merged.
- Run smoke tests against affected regions and services (example: curl health endpoints, run small inference job to validate throughput).

Capacity Planning (long-term):
1. Monthly cadence: capacity-planning working group meets on the 1st Tuesday of each month.
2. Inputs: observed utilization, growth forecast (product), queued requests, customer commitments (Dedicated contracts), and model onboarding plans.
3. Outputs: region-level reserved capacity targets, ondemand burst sizing, and budget requests for reserved instances where appropriate.
4. Metrics to track: per-region GPU-hours, spot failure rate, pre-warm hit-rate, cold-start latency.

Operational Playbooks (common scenarios):
- Scenario: Sudden customer surge in eu-west-1 (pending pods > 20)
  1. Acknowledge alert and assign primary owner.
  2. Increase region ASG desired capacity by +20 or enable ondemand burst.
  3. If quick scale fails due to quota, shift traffic to us-west-2 fallback and notify customer success.
  4. Open follow-up ticket to analyze root cause and consider pre-warming for high-traffic customers.

- Scenario: ENI attach failures during scale-up in us-east-1
  1. Inspect instance type and current ENI utilization.
  2. Reduce pods-per-node or move to instance type with higher ENI density.
  3. If subnet exhaustion: create additional subnet in overlay and update IaC overlay to include it.

Diagnostics and Useful Commands:
- Check pending GPU pods: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep Pending | grep gpu
- Describe scheduling failure: kubectl describe pod <pod-name>
- Check node GPU utilization: kubectl top nodes | grep gpu
- Terraform plan for region overlay: cd infra/overlays/us-west-2 && terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars
- Re-run CI pipeline: gh workflow run terraform-plan-apply.yml --ref hotfix/<branch>

Postmortem and Documentation Requirements:
- For any incident that meets P0 or P1 criteria, create a postmortem within 72 hours and link it here under related_pages. Include: timeline, root cause, impact, mitigations, follow-ups (owner + due date).

Links and references:
- Infra module list: infra/modules/ (GPU pool, networking, cloud_accounts)
- GPU fleet guide: /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026
- CI pipeline docs: /confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/terraform-ci-cd-playbook

Appendix: Quick checklist (start here when paged)
- [ ] Acknowledge PagerDuty and create incident channel
- [ ] Identify affected regions and services
- [ ] Check for scheduling errors and cloud quota errors
- [ ] Attempt scale-up (ASG / Karpenter limits / ondemand burst)
- [ ] If scale fails -> re-route traffic to fallback regions or reserved pools
- [ ] If applied emergency console changes -> commit to Terraform and open PR
- [ ] Post-incident: run postmortem and update this runbook if necessary
